summary: Lists the design principles, scope and requirements for version 2 of the Electronic Commerce Modeling Language, covering XML syntax, data model, format and payment processing. It is informational.

eli5.summary: This planning note says what an improved online-checkout form language should do, such as how it handles data and payments.

subtitle: Planning document for an XML language to describe electronic payment transactions.

tldr.problem: Electronic commerce needs a standard way to describe payment transaction data that covers multiple payment methods and works with both business-to-consumer and business-to-business transactions.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3505 lists design principles and requirements for version 2 of the Electronic Commerce Modeling Language, which will define XML syntax and a data model for payment information.
tldr.outcome: This is a requirements document that guides the development of ECML v2, extending the earlier HTML form-based version to support additional payment types like ACH, electronic checks, and mobile payments.

facts.label: New payment types
facts.value: ACH, electronic check, mobile phone, PDA

facts.label: Predecessor
facts.value: ECML v1.1 (RFC 3106, HTML form field names)

today: RFC 3505 is an Informational document describing the requirements that guided the development of ECML v2. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Introduction and Background
sections.content:
ECML (Electronic Commerce Modeling Language) version 2 will define the syntax for Payment Processing Objects using XML. The document covers requirements for XML syntax, data model, format, and payment processing across multiple transaction types: credit cards, electronic checks, lines of credit, Automated Clearing House (ACH), mobile phone payments, and PDA payments.

ECML v1.1 was developed by the ECML Alliance as a set of HTML form field names. Control passed to the IETF, which is now extending it to XML. The fields were initially based on the W3C P3P base data schema and extend to include fields from the P3P E-Commerce specification and the ISO 8583 financial transaction standard.
sections.eli5: ECML is a set of standard names for the fields in an online checkout form. Version 2 will use XML instead of HTML and handle more kinds of payments.

sections.title: Design Principles and Scope
sections.content:
The specification must cover the fields needed to process payments between consumer and merchant or between two businesses. Eight core design principles guide ECML v2:

The standard must keep new fields to a minimum, maintain backward compatibility with ECML v1.1 as a superset, and increase flexibility to include ACH, mobile, PDA and electronic check payments. It should allow a common DTD with enterprise resource planning systems and work with Business-to-Business payment mechanisms including B2B wallets and marketplaces. The specification should include a usage guide and follow broad Web design principles of decentralization, URIs, modularity and extensibility.
sections.eli5: The new version must be compatible with the old one, support more payment types, and work with both consumer and business payments.

sections.title: Requirements for Version 2
sections.content:
ECML v2 must cover six payment processing elements: Cost, Receipt, Currency, Card, Payment, and Bank/Telco. It must support all payment types from ECML 1.1 plus four new types: Automated Clearing House, electronic check, mobile phone payments, and PDA payments.

A well-formed DTD and schema must be developed for the new fields. The specification should be tested against representative ACH, electronic check and mobile phone payment setups. It must be compared for completeness against ECML v1.1, P3P E-Commerce guidance, ISO 8583 financial transaction messages, and ebXML.
sections.eli5: Version 2 needs to handle six kinds of information (like cost and payment method) and support five different ways to pay, including newer methods like mobile phones.

sections.title: Implementation Considerations and Issues
sections.content:
The document lists specific requirements received from early ECML v1.1 users. The Last Name field minimum must increase to at least 22 characters. Internationalization support needs improvement. Telephone number and email fields should be longer to accommodate global formats.

A new "translation field" should map existing application fields to ECML-specified fields. This mapping field (normally hidden in HTML) would allow ECML support without changes to existing code; the ECML code fills in existing fields based on which ECML field they correspond to.

Many ECML fields contain sensitive payment and personal information. The specification must include warnings and suggested safeguards, though ECML itself does not add security mechanisms. Security depends on the transmission infrastructure (such as TLS) and on applications that store or handle the information.
sections.eli5: Names and phone numbers need more room. There's a way to let new systems and old systems work together. And everything must warn developers that payment data is sensitive.
